Ran exact-quote follow-ups for "Ever since I was a child...consciousness behind the universe," "Any man can stay sober in a desert," and "When a computer creates art" to resolve local context; these showed first-person speech or character thought embedded within third-person narration.
person_note: The sole clearly diagnostic Goodreads scene quote uses sustained external narration of Langdon, while nearly all other quotations are dialogue, epigraphs, aphorisms, or local thoughts. In particular, q01565 is Langdon speaking and q01566 is Ávila's thought, so their first-person language does not create a first-person narrative strand. The authorized opening independently sustains third-person narration across different focal characters, and two whole-book descriptions identify an omniscient third-person structure with shifting focalization. No credible evidence indicates sustained first- or second-person base sections; the main limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers only the opening, mitigated by the whole-book structural sources and the diagnostic Goodreads scene.
